source.title: Commentary Critical and Explanatory on the Whole Bible
source.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset and David Brown
source.edition: CCEL expanded electronic edition of the 1871 public-domain text

entries.heading: Verse 1
entries.text: Pr 10:1-32 . Here begins the second part of the book, Pr 10:1-22:16 , which, with the third, Pr 22:16-25:28 , contains series of proverbs whose sense is complete in one or two verses, and which, having no logical connection, admit of no analysis. The parallelisms of Pr 10:1-15:33 are mostly antithetic; and those of Pr 16:1-22:16 , synthetic. The evidences of art in the structure are very clear, and indicate, probably, a purpose of facilitating the labor of memorizing.

entries.heading: 2. Treasures . . . nothing
entries.text: 2. Treasures . . . nothing --that is, Ill-gotten gains give no true happiness (compare Pr 4:17; Mt 6:19 ). righteousness --especially beneficence ( Ps 112:9 ). death --the greatest of all evils.
3. (Compare Ps 37:16-20 ). The last clause is better: "He will repel the greedy desires of the wicked."

entries.heading: 4. slack
entries.text: 4. slack --literally, "deceitful," failing of its purpose (compare Ho 7:16 ). maketh rich --(compare Pr 10:22 ).

entries.heading: 5. son
entries.text: 5. son --as Pr 1:8, 10 , and often. sleepeth --in indolence, and not for rest. causeth shame --literally, "is base" (compare Pr 14:35; 17:2 ).

entries.heading: 6. Blessings
entries.text: 6. Blessings --literally, "Praises." The last clause is better: "The mouth of the wicked covereth (or concealeth) violence (or mischievous devices)" to be executed in due time ( Ps 5:9; 10:7; Ro 3:14 ), and hence has no praises (compare Pr 10:11 ).

entries.heading: 7. blessed
entries.text: 7. blessed --literally, "for a blessing," or praise. shall rot --literally, "be worm-eaten," useless and disgusting.

entries.heading: 8. wise,
entries.text: 8. wise, &c.--(compare Pr 9:8, 9, 16 ), opposed to prating fool --or, "fool of lips of wicked language." fall --headlong, suddenly.

entries.heading: 9. perverteth his ways
entries.text: 9. perverteth his ways --acts deceitfully. known --discovered and punished.
10. Two vices contrasted; hypocrisy, or insinuating evil against one ( Pr 6:13; Ps 35:19 ), and rashness of speech. In each case, the results are on the evildoers.

entries.heading: 11. a well
entries.text: 11. a well --or, "source" of good to himself and others ( Joh 7:37, 38 ). On last clause, see on Pr 10:6 .

entries.heading: 12. strifes
entries.text: 12. strifes --or, "litigations." covereth --by forgiveness and forbearance.

entries.heading: 13. In the lips . . . found
entries.text: 13. In the lips . . . found --hence, not beaten, as the wicked-speaking fool. void of understanding -- ( Pr 6:32; 7:7 ).

entries.heading: 14. lay up knowledge
entries.text: 14. lay up knowledge --that is, as treasures for good use. mouth . . . destruction --or, "as to the mouth," &c., destruction is near; they expose themselves to evil by prating.
15. Both by trusting in "uncertain riches" ( 1Ti 6:17 ), or by the evils of poverty ( Pr 30:9 ), men, not fearing God, fall into dangers.
16. The industry of the righteous is alone truly successful, while the earnings of the wicked tempt and lead to sin.

entries.heading: 17. keepeth
entries.text: 17. keepeth --observes ( Pr 3:18; 4:22 ). refuseth --or, "turns from reproof," which might direct him aright.
18. Both vices must one day be known and punished, and hence their folly.
19. Much speech involves risk of sin; hence the wisdom of restraining the tongue ( Ps 39:1; Jas 1:26 ).
20. Right speech is the fruit of a good heart, but the wicked show theirs to be useless.
21. Fools not only fail to benefit others, as do the righteous, but procure their own ruin (compare Pr 10:11, 17; Ho 4:6 ).

entries.heading: 22. it maketh,
entries.text: 22. it maketh, &c.--"it" is emphatic. Riches from God are without the sorrow of ill-gotten wealth (compare Ec 2:21-23; 1Ti 6:9, 10, 17 ).
23. Sin is the pleasure of the wicked; wisdom that of the good.

entries.heading: 24. it
entries.text: 24. it --the very thing. The wicked get dreaded evil; the righteous, desired good.
25. (Compare Ps 1:4; 37:9, 10, 36 ). righteous . . . foundation --well laid and firm ( Mt 7:24, 25 ).
26. that is, causes vexation.
27. (Compare Pr 9:11; Ps 55:23 ).

entries.heading: 28. gladness
entries.text: 28. gladness --in confidence of realizing it. expectation . . . perish --in disappointment.

entries.heading: 29. The way,
entries.text: 29. The way, &c.--that is, God's providence sustains the righteous and overthrows the wicked ( Ho 14:9 ).
30. (Compare Pr 12:3; Ps 37:9-11; 102:28 ). earth --or, "land of promise."

entries.heading: 31. bringeth forth
entries.text: 31. bringeth forth --literally, "germinates" as a plant. froward --(Compare Pr 2:12, 14 ). cut off --as an unproductive plant.

entries.heading: 32. know
entries.text: 32. know --regard and provide for ( Ps 1:6 ). frowardness --all kinds of deceit and ill-nature. The word is plural.
